summary: A 1939 two-story NPS frame lookout in Glacier's Waterton Valley, used for fire watch until about 1972 and now reached by a long backcountry hike from Goat Haunt.

facts.design: Two-story NPS frame cab, standardized lookout design in the Rustic Style

access.note: Backcountry building in Glacier reached on foot from Goat Haunt. Sources do not say whether visitors may enter the cab; the register says backcountry rangers use it.

visit.trail_note: About 9.6 miles on foot from Goat Haunt (4.2 miles to the lookout trail junction, then 5.4 miles), with river crossings and 17 switchbacks; a trip report describes a tour boat from Waterton, Canada to Goat Haunt.

events.note: Project began 23 May 1939 per the nomination file; register photos show it under construction in 1939 and completed by 1940
firelookout.com says abandoned in 1972; the register says not used much for fire detection after 1972 but still used by backcountry rangers
1988 National Register nomination form prepared; the park found the lookout eligible under Criteria A and C (not a listing)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives Flathead County, which matches the record; firelookout.com says Glacier County.
The register gives 7,000 ft (2,134 m), matching the record's 2133.6 m; firelookout.com and SummitPost give 7,100 ft. The 100-ft difference is not explained by the sources.
All sources date construction to 1939. Photo captions show work under way in 1939 and a finished lookout in 1940.
The register says backcountry rangers still use the lookout; SummitPost lists it as standing but abandoned. Both agree it still stands.

notes_for_editor: The NPS nomination PDF is OCR text, and the 'last of eleven' sentence is garbled, so the quote is a clean fragment. Staffing 'unstaffed' since 1972 is inferred from 'not used for fire detection much after 1972'. Current public access is unconfirmed. The visit detail rests on one SummitPost trip report. No notable fires found in sources read. No new photos: the NHLR photos are all rights reserved. The NPS PDF also has a passage saying the lookout is eligible 'under the Multiple Resource Submission', which sits uneasily with the letter's 'not included with the submission'. The OCR is poor, so this is flagged rather than resolved. The SummitPost page header gives 9.7 miles; the story uses the trip report's own 4.2 + 5.4 miles, about 9.6.
